question: Why is a parked car so hard to push on a level road?
answer: A car has a lot of inertia: it resists any change in its motion, so getting it rolling takes a big force. On a level road you are not lifting it, because the road holds its weight. Swapping it for a cart gives the same push, but the car barely creeps.
move: Weight makes a thing hard to lift; inertia makes it hard to push.
